newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers still bullish on US debt - MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers still bullish on US debt - MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers extended durations of their U.S. debt portfolios over the past week, an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey said.
In a separate portion of the survey, MCM asked the 38 participants if the Federal Reserve will tighten short-term interest rates at the next monetary policy meeting on July 1-2.
Sixty percent of the respondents said yes, 20 percent said no, and the remainder were "fence sitters," MCM said.

MCM MoneyWatch Inc vice president Astrid Adolfson, who conducts the weekly investor survey, said: "Money was put out the curve as can be seen in a decrease in the overweightings for the one- to 10-year sector, but there was an increase in the 10-plus year area."
The survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 108.2 percent in the week ending June 2 from 108.1 in the prior survey week ended May 19.
The survey was postponed due to the Memorial Day holiday in the week ended May 26.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 37 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," compared with 39 percent the prior survey week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" rose to 12 percent, against 8.0 percent the week ended May 19.
Fifty-one percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market.
Cash as a percentage of assets rose to 3.09 percent, up slightly from 3.07 percent registered the previous survey week.

The survey showed 30 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, modestly higher from the 29-percent in the previous survey week, while 8.0 percent underweighted it. The remaining 62 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 41 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 11 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
